name: dbt Labs, Inc. (formerly Fishtown Analytics; now 'Fivetran + dbt Labs')
origin_detail: Founded 2016 in Philadelphia as Fishtown Analytics, a data-analytics consulting firm, by Tristan Handy, Drew Banin and Connor McArthur; dbt began as an internal consulting tool; renamed dbt Labs in 2021; combined with Fivetran (joint brand 'Fivetran + dbt Labs' in use by Sep 2026)
openness_notes: Open core: dbt Core has been Apache-2.0 while dbt Cloud is proprietary SaaS. By Sep 2026 the Python engine (dbt v1) and the Rust Fusion engine (dbt v2) were both described as Apache-2.0-licensed. Whether Fusion was first released in 2025 under a source-available licence (reported elsewhere as ELv2) could not be confirmed from fetched pages.

license_history.license: Apache-2.0 (dbt v1 Python engine and dbt v2 Fusion Rust engine)
license_history.note: Core and Fusion merged into one engine with two versions; both 'remain Apache 2.0-licensed and security-supported'

exit_events.note: By 16 Sep 2026 the companies issued releases as 'Fivetran + dbt Labs' with a shared chief product officer; announcement date, structure, valuation and closing date were not confirmed in fetched pages

risk_events: 2022 peak valuation ($4.2B, Series D led by Altimeter) not refreshed by any later priced round found
Consolidation: combined with ELT vendor Fivetran (joint brand by Sep 2026), ending independence
Strategic tension between free dbt Core and paid dbt Cloud, and new Rust engine (Fusion) licensing (2025 status unverified)
robustness: dbt is the de facto standard for SQL transformation (100,000+ data teams in 2026; ~9,000 companies on open-source dbt in Mar 2022) and the Apache-2.0 engine can be forked or self-hosted. The company is now part of a larger Fivetran combination, which adds scale but removes independence.
physical_science_relevance: Low directly; dbt is used in research data warehouses (e.g. lab LIMS/ELN analytics) to version and test SQL transformations.
openness_effect_assessment: Open-sourcing an internal consulting tool created a professional community ('analytics engineering') and a standard that drove rapid growth (paying customers tripled to ~1,800 in 2021; revenue up 6x in 2021) and a $4.2B valuation. Monetizing via dbt Cloud proved harder than adoption, and the company ultimately combined with Fivetran; as of 2026 both engines are Apache-2.0, so openness has not been retracted.
key_takeaway: dbt Labs turned a consultancy's open-source tool into an industry standard and a $4.2B (2022) valuation, then consolidated with Fivetran rather than IPO. It shows how a permissive, community-defined standard can create large value for the ecosystem while the originating company's standalone outcome is merger rather than independence.
